title: Cold rebuild: Group anagrams
summary: Rebuild Group anagrams from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Group anagrams** in *Counting and grouping with Dictionary*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: Which word is most common? What does this print?
code: foreach (var w in "to be or not to be to".Split(' '))
steps.explain: `to` appears three times; the distinct words are `to`, `be`, `or`, `not`.

steps.title: Rebuild Group anagrams cold
prompt: - Words with the same letters go in the same group.
- Groups appear in the order their **first** word appears; words inside a group keep their input order.
A `Dictionary<string, List<string>>` adds keys in insertion order when nothing is removed, so `groups.Values` comes out in first-seen order.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
